Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) suffer from severe voltage 
loss, which significantly limits the enhancement of photovoltaic performance. 
Here, 4-fluoro-phenylethylammonium iodide (FPEAI) is used as a dual-
functional agent for oriented crystallization and comprehensive passivation 
of WBG PSCs. The additive of FPEAI promotes crystals to grow along with 
the (100) orientation with improved crystallinity and to spontaneously form 
Ruddlesden–Popper 2D perovskite on the grain boundary and surface of 3D 
crystals, which can passivate defects and protect the perovskite film from 
moisture erosion as well as suppressed ion migration. In addition, the 2D/3D 
heterostructure induces a matched energy-level alignment, which mitigates 
the detrimental interfacial charge recombination at the interface of the 3D 
perovskite and hole transport layer. Consequently, the modified WBG PSCs 
exhibit an improved open-circuit voltage to 1.3 V and a fill factor of 77.8%, 
leading to a remarkable power conversion efficiency of 19.1% with negligible 
hysteresis. Furthermore, the WBG PSCs maintain 85% of the original effi-
ciency after 1000 h in air, demonstrating outstanding humidity stability. This 
work indicates that FPEAI can be used as a dual-functional agent to signifi-
cantly enhance the efficiency of WBG PSCs.

2. Results and Discussion
The composition of WBG perovskite in this work is 
Cs0.2FA0.8Pb(I0.7Br0.3)3, deposited by a one-step method.[20] 
Its optical bandgap (Eg) is ≈1.75 eV, as shown in Figure S1 in 
the Supporting Information. For the FPEAI-added sample, 1.5 
mol% FAI was substituted by FPEAI in the perovskite pre-
cursor. The FPEAI/IPA solution was spun cast onto the WBG 
perovskite film to obtain the passivated film. For simplicity, the 
films of pristine Cs0.2FA0.8Pb(I0.7Br0.3)3, FPEAI-added Cs0.2FA0.8
Pb(I0.7Br0.3)3, FPEAI interface treatment for pristine Cs0.2FA0.8P
b(I0.7Br0.3)3, and synergetic strategy are named as Control, Addi-
tive, Passivation, and A&P, respectively. The schematic illus-
tration of the perovskite film deposition process is depicted in 
Figure 1. As can be seen, the synergetic mechanism of FPEAI is 
to modulate crystallization and in-situ form 2D/3D heterostruc-
ture perovskite, as deduced by the following studies.
Top-view scanning electron microscopy (SEM) measurement 
was conducted to investigate the surface topography. As shown 
in Figure 2a,b, the films have dense and pinhole-free mor-
phology. With adding FPEAI, the grain size of samples becomes 
smaller. Figure 2e shows the corresponding size distribution of 
the two samples. As can be seen, the average grain size of the 
Control film is ≈248 nm, whereas the Additive film is decreased 
to 175 nm. This observation implies that the FPEAI influences 
the crystal growth mode. After FPEAI interface treatment, the 
3D WBG perovskite film was covered by the in situ fabricated 
2D perovskite as shown in Figure 2c,d. An obvious grain-coars-
ening process can be seen and should be attributed to the ther-
modynamically spontaneous Ostwald ripening process.[21] The 
A&P film exhibits a flatter surface than the Passivation film, 
and the density of grain boundary is relatively reduced, which 
can be explained by the cross-sectional SEM (Figure  2f). The 
atomic force microscopy (AFM) (seen in Figure S2 in the Sup-
porting Information) images show a reduced root-mean-square 
surface roughness (RMS), demonstrating the smoother mor-
phology of the synergetic strategy. To confirm the presence of 
2D Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) perovskite, transmission electron 
microscopy (TEM) was used to analyze the A&P perovskite 
film. Figure  2g shows a chunk of the A&P sample scratched 
from the substrate. One of the typical regions is magnified 
and the corresponding highlighted regions I (perovskite grain) 
and II (grain boundary) are shown in Figure  2h,i. As can be 
seen, the d-spacing of region I can be measured to be 3.08 Å, 
matched with the (200) crystal plane of the 3D WBG perovskite. 
The region II shows a larger d-spacing at the grain boundary to 
be 4.1 Å, which is consistent with the (004) plane of FPEA2PbI4 
(Table S1, Supporting Information). These results suggest that 
the observed 2D perovskites are formed at the grain boundary 
or the upper surface, which can effectively passivate the defect.

3. Conclusion
In this work, we report a synergetic strategy to simultaneously 
improve the crystallinity and passivate the defects at grain 
boundary and interface by using alkylammonium salt 4-fluoro-
phenylethylammonium iodide (FPEAI) as a dual-functional 
agent. In this synergistic strategy, the FPEAI modulates the 
crystallization of 3D WBG perovskite film and reduces trap den-
sity, and suppresses nonradiative recombination, leading to a 
remarkable PCE up to 19.07% with significantly enhanced VOC to 
1.30 V and FF to 77.8%. On a large-area device of 1 cm2, a PCE of 
15.01% with a high VOC of 1.29 V can be achieved, indicating the 
potential for scale-up PSCs. Furthermore, the 2D perovskite at 
the grain boundary and surface endows the cells with enhanced 
hydrophobic property and long-term stability. As a result, the 
modified devices retained 85% of their initial efficiencies under 
a relative humidity of 30% for 1000 h. Our study provides new 
insight into high-efficiency and stabilized WBG PSCs.
4. Experimental Section
Raw Materials: All the materials and chemicals were used without 
further purification. SnO2 nanoparticle was purchased from Alfa Aesar. 
Spiro-OMeTAD (99.8%) was obtained from Lumtech. 4-tert-butylpyridine 
(tBP, >96%), lead (II) iodide (PbI2, 99.99%), lead bromide (PbBr2, 
99.99%), cesium iodide (CsI, 99.99%), formamidinium iodide (FAI, 
≥99.5%), and 4-fluoro-phenylethylammonium iodide (FPEAI, ≥99.5%) 
were ordered from Xi’an Polymer Light Technology Corp. All the solvents 
were purchased from Sigma Aldrich.
Fabrication of WBG PSCs: Indium-doped tin oxide (ITO) glasses were 
precleaned with detergent, acetone, and ethanol for 15 min each. The 
cleaned ITO was treated with UV ozone (UVO) for 15 min to remove the 
organic residue and improve the wettability. The SnO2 dispersion was 
(diluted at 1:3 with deionized water) deposited on the ITO substrate at a 
rate of 4000 r.p.m. for 20 s, followed by annealing at 180 °C for 20 min. 
The SnO2/ITO/glass substrates were treated with UVO for 15 min and 
then transferred to the N2 glove box. For the Cs0.2FA0.8Pb(I0.7Br0.3)3 
composition, 52.0 mg CsI, 137.6 mg FAI, 253.6 mg PbI2 and 165.2 mg 
PbBr2 were dissolved in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO)/dimethylformamide 
(DMF) mixed solvent (1:3 v/v). To synthesize the Additive perovskite, 
1.5 mol% FAI was substituted by FPEAI. The films were deposited at 
1000 r.p.m. for 10 s and 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. 100 µL chlorobenzene was 
dropped on the film after 30 s. Then the film was annealed at 100 °C 
for 30 min. For FPEAI treatment, the FPEAI/IPA solution was spin-
coated onto the perovskite surface at 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. Subsequently, 
72.3 mg spiro-OMeTAD, 17.5 µL of LiTFSI (520 mg mL−1 in acetonitrile), 
and 29 µL tBP were dissolved in 1 mL chlorobenzene, then the solution 
was spin-coated onto the perovskite film at 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. Finally, 
100 nm Ag was thermal evaporated onto the spiro-OMeTAD layer, the 
active area of the device is determined by a shadow mask of 0.14 cm2.
Characterizations: The crystallographic characterizations were tested by 
X-ray diffraction (XRD) using PANalytical B.V. X-ray diffractometer with 
Cu Kα radiation under operating conditions of 40 kV and 40 mA. The 
morphology of the films was observed by SEM (FEI INSPECT F50, U.S.A.). 
AFM images were obtained by AFM (KEYSIGHT Technologies 7500). 
TEM was performed by FEI Tecnai G2 F20. XPS and UPS were taken with 
an XPS/UPS system (Thermo scientific, Al Kα radiation). The UV–vis 
spectra were measured using a UV-3600 spectrophotometer (Shimadzu 
Corporation). PL and TRPL were performed with an FLS980 (Edinburgh 
Instruments Ltd). Current density–voltage (J–V) curves of WBG PSCs 
were performed using a Keithley 2400 Source Meter under standard AM 
1.5G illumination (100 mW cm−2, SS-F5-3A). The corresponding EQE 
spectrum was measured by a PVE300 photovoltaic system.

stability is tested under a relative humidity of 30%± 10% without 
encapsulation at room temperature. A&P devices retain 85% 
of their original PCEs after 1000 h, whilst the Control devices 
maintain 70% under the same conditions. This result indicates 
the improved moisture stability with this proposed synergetic 
strategy via modulating the crystallinity and defect passivation.
3. Conclusion
In this work, we report a synergetic strategy to simultaneously 
improve the crystallinity and passivate the defects at grain 
boundary and interface by using alkylammonium salt 4-fluoro-
phenylethylammonium iodide (FPEAI) as a dual-functional 
agent. In this synergistic strategy, the FPEAI modulates the 
crystallization of 3D WBG perovskite film and reduces trap den-
sity, and suppresses nonradiative recombination, leading to a 
remarkable PCE up to 19.07% with significantly enhanced VOC to 
1.30 V and FF to 77.8%. On a large-area device of 1 cm 2, a PCE of 
15.01% with a high VOC of 1.29 V can be achieved, indicating the 
potential for scale-up PSCs. Furthermore, the 2D perovskite at 
the grain boundary and surface endows the cells with enhanced 
hydrophobic property and long-term stability. As a result, the 
modified devices retained 85% of their initial efficiencies under 
a relative humidity of 30% for 1000 h. Our study provides new 
insight into high-efficiency and stabilized WBG PSCs.
4. Experimental Section
Raw Materials: All the materials and chemicals were used without 
further purification. SnO 2 nanoparticle was purchased from Alfa Aesar. 
Spiro-OMeTAD (99.8%) was obtained from Lumtech. 4-tert-butylpyridine 
(tBP, >96%), lead (II) iodide (PbI 2, 99.99%), lead bromide (PbBr 2, 
99.99%), cesium iodide (CsI, 99.99%), formamidinium iodide (FAI, 
≥99.5%), and 4-fluoro-phenylethylammonium iodide (FPEAI, ≥99.5%) 
were ordered from Xi’an Polymer Light Technology Corp. All the solvents 
were purchased from Sigma Aldrich.
Fabrication of WBG PSCs: Indium-doped tin oxide (ITO) glasses were 
precleaned with detergent, acetone, and ethanol for 15 min each. The 
cleaned ITO was treated with UV ozone (UVO) for 15 min to remove the 
organic residue and improve the wettability. The SnO 2 dispersion was 
(diluted at 1:3 with deionized water) deposited on the ITO substrate at a 
rate of 4000 r.p.m. for 20 s, followed by annealing at 180  °C for 20 min. 
The SnO2/ITO/glass substrates were treated with UVO for 15 min and 
then transferred to the N 2 glove box. For the Cs 0.2FA0.8Pb(I0.7Br0.3)3 
composition, 52.0 mg CsI, 137.6 mg FAI, 253.6 mg PbI 2 and 165.2 mg 
PbBr2 were dissolved in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO)/dimethylformamide 
(DMF) mixed solvent (1:3 v/v). To synthesize the Additive perovskite, 
1.5 mol% FAI was substituted by FPEAI. The films were deposited at 
1000 r.p.m. for 10 s and 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. 100 µ L chlorobenzene was 
dropped on the film after 30 s. Then the film was annealed at 100  °C 
for 30 min. For FPEAI treatment, the FPEAI/IPA solution was spin-
coated onto the perovskite surface at 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. Subsequently,  
72.3 mg spiro-OMeTAD, 17.5 µ L of LiTFSI (520 mg mL−1 in acetonitrile), 
and 29 µL tBP were dissolved in 1 mL chlorobenzene, then the solution 
was spin-coated onto the perovskite film at 4000 r.p.m. for 30 s. Finally, 
100 nm Ag was thermal evaporated onto the spiro-OMeTAD layer, the 
active area of the device is determined by a shadow mask of 0.14 cm 2.
Characterizations: The crystallographic characterizations were tested by 
X-ray diffraction (XRD) using PANalytical B.V. X-ray diffractometer with 
Cu Kα  radiation under operating conditions of 40 kV and 40 mA. The 
morphology of the films was observed by SEM (FEI INSPECT F50, U.S.A.). 
AFM images were obtained by AFM (KEYSIGHT Technologies 7500). 
TEM was performed by FEI Tecnai G2 F20. XPS and UPS were taken with 
an XPS/UPS system (Thermo scientific, Al Kα  radiation). The UV–vis 
spectra were measured using a UV-3600 spectrophotometer (Shimadzu 
Corporation). PL and TRPL were performed with an FLS980 (Edinburgh 
Instruments Ltd). Current density–voltage (J –V) curves of WBG PSCs 
were performed using a Keithley 2400 Source Meter under standard AM 
1.5G illumination (100 mW cm −2, SS-F5-3A). The corresponding EQE 
spectrum was measured by a PVE300 photovoltaic system.
